root_cause.text: The f2fs GC readahead path in ra_data_block() could submit a read BIO for an encrypted page cache folio that had already been updated and marked Uptodate by a prior move_data_block GC migration, causing end_read to hit VM_BUG_ON on an already-uptodate folio.
root_cause.evidence: The fix adds `if (folio_test_uptodate(efolio)) goto put_encrypted_page;` before `f2fs_submit_page_bio(&fio)`, and the commit message explicitly describes the same page being moved from A→B and then B→C, with `ra_data_block` unnecessarily reading block B again after the page was “marked as uptodate,” leading to `VM_BUG_ON_FOLIO(folio_test_uptodate(folio))`.

intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added before calling f2fs_submit_page_bio(): if folio_test_uptodate(efolio) is true, execution jumps directly to the existing put_encrypted_page label.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this skips submitting a page read BIO for an encrypted folio that is already marked uptodate, avoiding redundant I/O and reusing the existing cleanup path instead of rereading data.

That redundant read could later trigger end_read on an already-uptodate folio, matching the described root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full introduction of the GC readahead path for encrypted blocks in `ra_data_block()` and the corresponding consumption path in `move_data_block()`. The vulnerable construct is present: `ra_data_block()` grabs a page cache page with `page = f2fs_grab_cache_page(mapping, index, true);` and then unconditionally submits a read BIO via `err = f2fs_submit_page_bio(&fio);` after setting `fio.page = page;` and `fio.encrypted_page = ... META_MAPPING(sbi), dn.data_blkaddr ...`. There is no check to avoid submitting readahead for a page/folio that may already have been updated and marked Uptodate by prior GC migration activity. In `move_data_block()`, the code explicitly detects an already-updated meta page: `if (PageUptodate(mpage)) { memcpy(...); updated = true; } ... if (updated) goto write_page;`, which shows that pages associated with the same old block can already be uptodate before the read completes. That matches the root-cause race: readahead can be in flight against a page cache folio that has already been updated by `move_data_block()`. The fix is not present because there is no guard in `ra_data_block()` to skip BIO submission when the target page/folio is already Uptodate or otherwise updated, and no synchronization preventing stale readahead against an already-updated encrypted page cache folio.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact logic changed to prevent the race in the GC encrypted-page path. The commit adds two key protections in `move_encrypted_block()`: (1) when `dn.data_blkaddr == NULL_ADDR`, it now executes `ClearPageUptodate(page);` before `goto put_out;`, which avoids leaving the page marked uptodate on this error/skip path; and (2) before using the encrypted page cached in the meta inode, it now explicitly waits with `f2fs_wait_on_page_writeback(page, DATA);` under the comment `don't cache encrypted data into meta inode until previous dirty data were writebacked to avoid racing between GC and flush.` This is precisely the kind of synchronization missing in the vulnerable behavior. Additionally, the code changes `f2fs_wait_on_page_writeback(fio.encrypted_page, META);` to `f2fs_wait_on_page_writeback(fio.encrypted_page, DATA);`, indicating corrected writeback-state handling for this encrypted GC path. Since the function already contains the added wait/cleanup logic that addresses the race, the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is present.
